# Bs: the stories first, then the spelling

Before the spelling, the story. **Bs** earns its restoration the old way — through what was actually told.

## The Stories That Carry the Name

**The Mask of the Midwife.** In the birth-chamber, the midwife donned the Bes-mask and danced his dance; his grimace drew the malign spirits’ attention onto himself and away from mother and child.  The Beset-amulets and the ‘Bes-chamber’ scenes of Deir el-Medina show the rite in domestic detail.

**The Dwarf Who Amuses the Gods.** The Westcar Papyrus’ wonder-tale of the dwarf Dedi, who dances and performs before the court, is read as Bes’ narrative shadow — the small deformed being whose skill and humour carry more power than the great.  Bes never speaks in the texts; he dances.

**Bes the Pantheos.** By the Late Period, Bes absorbed attributes of every major god — the wings of Horus, the crown of Amun, the snakes of Mehen — becoming the ‘Pantheos-Bes’, one dwarf wearing the whole pantheon’s power.  The type, with its many arms and animal faces, spread through the Greco-Roman world as an amulet-image.

## And Here Is What the Spelling Preserves


## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Bs
- **ASCII form:** bes
- **Meaning:** "The protector"
- **Domain of influence:** Protection, Childbirth, Joy
- **Pantheon:** Egyptian
- **Restoration:** ASCII-equivalent form
- **Original script:** 𓃀𓋴𓄜
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 89 of 597

## The Name Travels

Bes is the great syncretic absorber of the late period: Pantheos-Bes carries the attributes of all gods.  The Greeks equated him with their own apotropaic dwarves and the Pataikos figures, and Roman soldiers carried his amulets across the empire — the household god travelled as military gear.

## The Address It Earned

The temple of **Bs** stands at [/bes/](/bes/) — [lore](/bes/lore/), [scholars](/bes/scholars/), [patterns](/bes/patterns/) — because a name carrying this much story deserves more than a parking page. aSCII-equivalent form

## The Sources Are Open

The myths above are retold from the temple's record; the primary voices are in the [Sacred Texts](/texts/): [The Book of the Dead](/texts/book-of-the-dead/). Nothing in this file outranks them.

## The Emblems

The name does not travel alone. **Guardian of the Hearth** — His image watched over beds, births, and mirrors — the god of the domestic threshold.; **The Dancer-Demon** — His terrifying face and acrobatic dance frighten away the demons of childbirth and sleep.; **Lord of Childbirth** — The birth-brick and the Bes-mask of the midwife: he presided over every Egyptian child’s first hour.. Each emblem is filed in the temple's record with its own provenance, the same discipline the spelling gets.

## For the Voice

“BESS” The reconstructed line runs `/bɛs/ (conventional)` — the temple's pronunciation atlas carries the phonemes one by one.

## The Discipline It Answers To

This restoration belongs to Egyptian, a tradition that treated names as operational magic, not labels. The rules that govern it are not house style; they are the tradition's own scholarship, applied with the same care here as in any edition — and published, with the sources, so the file can be checked the way an edition can be checked. aSCII-equivalent form
